en: Ubayy ibn Ka'b narrated to us, he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) saying: While Musa (peace be upon him) was among his people reminding them of the Days of Allah—and the Days of Allah are His bounties and His trials—he said: "I do not know of any man on earth who is better or more knowledgeable than me." He said: So Allah revealed to him: "Indeed, I know better concerning what is good, or with whom it is; indeed, there is on earth a man who is more knowledgeable than you." Musa said: "O Lord, direct me to him." He said: So it was said to him: "Take a salted fish as provision, for he is wherever you lose the fish." He said: So he and his young companion set out until they reached the rock, but it was concealed from him, so he went on and left his young companion. The fish struggled in the water, and the water did not close over it, but became like an archway. He said: His young companion said, "Should I not catch up with the Prophet of Allah and inform him?" He said: But he was made to forget. When they had passed beyond, Musa said to his young companion: "Bring us our morning meal; we have certainly suffered fatigue from this journey of ours." He said: And fatigue did not touch them until they had passed beyond. He said: Then he remembered and said: "Did you see when we took refuge at the rock? Indeed, I forgot the fish, and none made me forget to mention it except Satan, and it took its course into the sea amazingly." Musa said: "That is what we were seeking!" So they retraced their footprints, following their tracks. He showed him the place of the fish, saying: "Right here was described to me." He said: So he went seeking, and behold, he came upon al-Khadir covered with a cloth, lying on the back of his neck—or he said: on the back of his head. Musa said: "Peace be upon you." So he uncovered the cloth from his face and said: "And upon you be peace; who are you?" He said: "I am Musa." He said: "And which Musa?" He said: "The Musa of the Children of Israel." He said: "What a coming! What brought you?" He said: "I have come that you may teach me of what you have been taught of sound judgment." He said: "Indeed, you will never be able to have patience with me, and how can you have patience over that which you have not encompassed in knowledge? It is something I have been commanded to do; when you see it, you will not be patient." Musa said: "You will find me, if Allah wills, patient, and I will not disobey you in any matter." He said: "Then if you follow me, do not ask me about anything until I make mention of it to you." So they set out until, when they embarked upon the ship, he damaged it. He said: He leaned over it and damaged it. Musa (peace be upon him) said to him: "Have you damaged it to drown its people? You have certainly done a grave thing!" He said: "Did I not say that you would never be able to have patience with me?" Musa said: "Do not blame me for what I forgot, and do not make my affair difficult for me." So they set out until they met some young boys playing. He said: He went towards one of them, without hesitation, and killed him. Thereupon Musa (peace be upon him) was terrified with extreme horror. He said: "Have you killed a pure soul without retaliation for a soul? You have certainly done an evil thing!" The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said at this point: "May the mercy of Allah be upon us and upon Musa! If only he had not been hasty, he would have seen marvelous things; but he felt ashamed before his companion. He said: 'If I ask you about anything after this, then do not keep company with me; you have received from me an excuse.' And if he had been patient, he would have seen marvelous things." He said: And whenever he mentioned one of the prophets, he began with himself: "May the mercy of Allah be upon us and upon my brother so-and-so; may the mercy of Allah be upon us." "Then they both set out until, when they came to the people of a mean town, they circulated among the gatherings and asked its people for food, but they refused to offer them hospitality. Then they found in it a wall about to collapse, so he restored it. Musa said: 'If you wished, you could have taken a payment for it.' He said: 'This is the parting between me and you,' and he took hold of his garment. He said: 'I will inform you of the interpretation of that over which you could not have patience: As for the ship, it belonged to poor people working at sea...' to the end of the verse. So when the one who commandeered ships came, he found it damaged and passed it by, and they repaired it with a piece of wood. 'And as for the boy, he was created on the day he was created as a disbeliever, and his parents were affectionate towards him; so had he grown up, he would have overburdened them with transgression and disbelief. So we intended that their Lord should substitute for them one better than him in purity and nearer in mercy. And as for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city, and beneath it was...' to the end of the verse."
